content:
The [Sleep Cycle Calculator](/sleep-cycle-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Find wake times aligned with five or six approximate 90-minute sleep cycles. Enter your bedtime (24-hour) and time to fall asleep and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Find wake times aligned with five or six approximate 90-minute sleep cycles. This free online sleep cycle calculator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Sleep Cycle Calculator

Start by typing or pasting your bedtime (24-hour), then entering your time to fall asleep (min). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Type or paste your bedtime (24-hour).
2. Enter your time to fall asleep (min).
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Wake time = bedtime + time to fall asleep + 90 minutes per cycle. Individual cycles vary.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Sleep Cycle Calculator](/sleep-cycle-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 22:30 bedtime plus 15 minutes to fall asleep gives a 6-cycle wake time of 07:45. Try the same figures in the [Sleep Cycle Calculator](/sleep-cycle-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Bedtime (24-hour): 22:30, Time to fall asleep: 15 min), the [Sleep Cycle Calculator](/sleep-cycle-calculator) returns Wake after 6 cycles: 07:45, Wake after 5 cycles: 06:15, Wake after 4 cycles: 04:45, Sleep onset: 22:45. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Check the units and labels before comparing results.
- Your entries stay in your browser and are not saved.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is this sleep cycle calculator free?

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up or installation required. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Sleep Cycle Calculator](/sleep-cycle-calculator) and start straight away.

### Are my entries stored?

No. Calculations run in your browser and the tool does not save your entries. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### What formula does the Sleep Cycle Calculator use?

Wake time = bedtime + time to fall asleep + 90 minutes per cycle. Individual cycles vary. You can see it in action in the [Sleep Cycle Calculator](/sleep-cycle-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Sleep Cycle Calculator?

Just Bedtime (24-hour) and Time to fall asleep. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
